kpis.label: Reference price
kpis.sub: Upside is shown against a range, not a price band: floor Rs 182.63 = Series B CCPS price paid in cash by Abakkus Four2eight Opportunities Fund on 17-Jul-2026 (Rs 100.0 cr, post split and bonus; p. 142); cap Rs 226.00 = the price of the promoters' secondary transfers on 10 to 21-Sep-2026, the latest priced transactions in the DRHP (pp. 102-104). Both are assumptions for a screen, not a band. The call rule uses the cap. The peer-median P/E of 121.5x (Dixon 48.6x, Amber 139.5x, PG Electroplast 121.5x, p. 135) is not used to set the reference.

focus.title: Bonus issue / share-count consistency
focus.detail: Bonus (1:1 on 28-Aug-2025, 3:1 on 20-Aug-2026) and the 1:2 split (Aug-2026) are applied in every EPS and price shown. Diluted EPS (Rs 9.04) equals basic EPS although 15,655,864 shares will be issued on CCPS conversion before the RHP; on the fully diluted pre-offer count of 84,197,664 shares FY26 EPS is Rs 7.77, 14% lower than the printed figure.

focus.title: Cash flow vs profit
focus.detail: Operating cash flow is negative in all three years: Rs -15.28 cr (FY24), Rs -64.11 cr (FY25), Rs -28.66 cr (FY26); cumulative Rs -108.05 cr against cumulative PAT of Rs 84.88 cr. FY26 absorbed Rs 97.26 cr in receivables and Rs 38.90 cr in inventory. The business grew from Rs 0.07 cr to Rs 1,221.76 cr of revenue in two years, so a build is expected, but no full working-capital cycle has yet been seen.

focus.title: Current vs deferred tax
focus.detail: Current tax Rs 14.54 cr on PBT Rs 79.63 cr = 18.3% in FY26 (6.7% in FY25); cumulative current tax Rs 16.37 cr on cumulative PBT Rs 104.88 cr = 15.6%, against the 25.17% statutory rate. Tax actually paid was Rs 5.26 cr in FY26; current tax liability stood at Rs 13.17 cr at 31-Mar-2026. The DRHP pages read do not give a reconciliation of the lower rate.

focus.title: Related-party capex & subsidiaries
focus.detail: Ekkaa Electronics Industries Pvt Ltd (EEIPL) was owned by the promoters Chandra Prakash Gupta and Madhuri Gupta until 29-Aug-2025. Sales to EEIPL were Rs 104.34 cr (21.0% of FY25 revenue) and Rs 75.81 cr (6.2% of FY26 revenue); purchases from it Rs 89.45 cr (18.0%) and Rs 36.30 cr (3.0%); loans taken from it Rs 170.85 cr in FY25 at Rs 8.40 cr interest. The promoters were paid in shares for 81.14% of EEIPL, valued at Rs 888 per Rs 10 share. The Sonipat site is leased from Gaurisuta Industries LLP (promoters are partners), rent Rs 0.03 m a month to Mar-2026 and Rs 0.50 m from Apr-2026. No proceeds go to a subsidiary or a promoter entity.

focus.title: Goodwill vs tangible equity
focus.detail: The restated accounts recognise a bargain-purchase capital reserve of Rs 2.04 cr on EEIPL and no goodwill; the unaudited pro-forma balance sheet shows goodwill of Rs 8.50 cr on the same acquisition (p. 381). The two treatments differ; the pro-forma goodwill would be 3.4% of net worth, the restated capital reserve 0.8%.

focus.title: Customer / supplier / geographic concentration
focus.detail: Demand: largest customer 16.86% of FY26 revenue (21.01% FY25), top 5 52.43%, top 10 65.77% (80.35% FY25); customer names withheld for want of consent. Supply: top supplier 46.94% of raw materials purchased (31.90% FY25), top 5 69.74%; imports Rs 802.57 cr = 76.2% of raw material purchases. LED televisions are 71.78% of revenue.

focus.title: Auditor qualifications / changes
focus.detail: M S K A & Associates LLP was appointed on 27-Nov-2025 to fill a casual vacancy caused by the death of the proprietor of the previous auditor, A. K. Khattar and Associates. FY24 and FY25 were audited on a special-purpose basis by the earlier auditor, with an emphasis-of-matter on the basis of preparation; MSKA restated them. The Form ADT-1 for the 5-year re-appointment from 1-Apr-2026 was pending when the DRHP was filed.

focus.title: CARO / audit trail
focus.detail: The audit trail was enabled and operated throughout FY26, but backup logs were kept only from 18-Feb-2026; periodic backups from 1-Apr-2025 to 17-Feb-2026 were taken without a retained log.

focus.title: Monitoring agency
focus.detail: The company will appoint a monitoring agency before the RHP (Reg 41); not yet named.

focus.title: Eligibility re-computation
focus.detail: The offer is made under Reg 6(2) because the issuer does not meet Reg 6(1)(b) (monetary assets are 0.92% of net tangible assets in FY26 and the operating-profit test fails in FY24 at Rs -1.20 cr): at least 75% of the net offer must go to QIBs or the offer fails and subscriptions are refunded. Net tangible assets Rs 253.25 cr, net worth Rs 251.53 cr and average operating profit Rs 48.78 cr at FY26.

focus.title: Lead-manager track record
focus.detail: Motilal Oswal: 14 IPOs listed in FY2026-27 so far, 21 in FY2025-26 and 7 in FY2024-25. Of the 21 FY26 issues, 6 closed below issue price at day 30 and 8 of the 19 with 180 days elapsed closed below at day 180. Shannon Advisors: 2 IPOs; Globtier Infotech (SME) was -36.95% at day 30 and -57.05% at day 180 (pp. 456-458). See Appendix B.

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -83.7% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause

focus.title: Valuation model guard
focus.detail: AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: Price band, offer price, final fresh/OFS share counts, offer expenses and general corporate purposes are all [●]; valuation uses reference prices of Rs 182.63 (floor) and Rs 226.00 (cap)

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: Financials run to 31-Mar-2026 (177 days before the DRHP date); no H1 FY27 data. Borrowings rose from Rs 308.75 cr at 31-Mar-2026 to Rs 396.14 cr at 31-Jul-2026, which the next audited period will show

focus.title: Data gap (high)
focus.detail: FY24 and FY25 are the company-only base (revenue Rs 0.07 cr and Rs 496.51 cr); FY26 includes EEIPL only from 29-Aug-2025. The unaudited pro-forma (FY26 Rs 1,263.14 cr, FY25 Rs 709.34 cr) is the only like-for-like view and carries no cash flow

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Names of the top 10 customers and top 10 suppliers are withheld for non-receipt of consents; the single supplier at 46.94% of purchases is not identified

focus.title: Data gap (medium)
focus.detail: Reconciliation of the 18.3% FY26 current-tax rate to the 25.17% statutory rate not located

comfort.title: Revaluation reserve
comfort.detail: No revaluation reserve in the restated reserves note.

comfort.title: Contingent liabilities
comfort.detail: No contingent liability requires disclosure at 31-Mar-2026. Litigation is one wage claim of Rs 93,433 and three direct-tax matters of Rs 0.99 m in all; the materiality threshold is Rs 15.50 m.

Lever 2 - implied WACC at terminal g
Lever 4 - required NWC % of revenue (steady state)

Promoter holding above the minimum, after the Rs 200 cr OFS (6 months from allotment, p. 105); at reference

bankers.name: Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors Limited
bankers.listed: Parent Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd is listed (NSE: MOTILALOFS); the merchant bank itself is a subsidiary - not independently verified

issues.issuer: National Stock Exchange of India Ltd

strengths: Revenue Rs 1,221.8 cr in FY26, pro-forma +78.1%, from Rs 0.07 cr in FY24 (pp. 74, 137)
EBITDA margin 9.37%, ROCE 18.0%, ROE 45.1%; interest cover 3.6x on EBIT Rs 100.9 cr (pp. 74, 137)
Installed capacity 5.20 m units, LED TV 2.82 m; about 5.5% share of Indian LED TV volume (pp. 245, 247)
Six product lines; non-LED TV products are 28.2% of revenue (p. 244)
Series B of Rs 100 cr from a Category I/II AIF in Jul-2026; litigation limited to a Rs 93,433 wage claim and Rs 0.99 m of tax matters (pp. 106, 142, 434-435)
weaknesses: Operating cash flow Rs -108.1 cr over FY24-26; 52.8% of receivables past due (pp. 75, 337)
Top 5 customers 52.4% of revenue; top supplier 46.9% of purchases; imports 76.2% (pp. 23, 29, 41)
Net debt Rs 296.0 cr, 2.58x EBITDA; 63% of FY26 borrowings are current (p. 73)
LED TVs are 71.8% of revenue; Noida TV line ran at 55.6% utilisation (pp. 244, 250)
Acquired subsidiary EEIPL lost Rs 5.75 cr in FY26 (EBITDA Rs -9.02 cr) (p. 138)
opportunities: Consumer-durables ODM market Rs 24,900 cr in FY26 to Rs 51,380 cr in FY30 (19.9% CAGR), issuer-commissioned (p. 245)
Unused capacity: 2.38 m units outside LED TVs, with cooktops at 10.5% and speakers at 2.3% utilisation (p. 250)
Ganaur cooler plant commissioned Jan-2026; blower coolers and fully automatic washers planned (pp. 243, 257)
Rs 225 cr of proceeds retires term loans at 7.15% to 9.35% and cash credit at repo + 2.5% to 3.75% (pp. 122-124)
threats: No long-term contracts with suppliers; raw materials are bought order by order, and the top supplier is 46.9% of purchases (pp. 29-30)
Rupee: unrealised exchange loss Rs 10.1 cr in FY26 with 76.2% of materials imported (pp. 41, 75)
Import-restriction risk on open cells, PCBs and motors (p. 41)
Listed peers are 4 to 40 times the issuer's revenue (Dixon Rs 48,873 cr against Rs 1,222 cr) (p. 135)

adjustments.item: Liabilities no longer required written back to other income
adjustments.reason: Other income of Rs 6.64 cr includes Rs 0.85 cr of liabilities written back, which did not recur in FY25 (nil); 1.1% of PBT. Not part of operating earnings.

adjustments.item: Interest subsidy under the UP Electronics Manufacturing Policy credited to other income
adjustments.reason: Rs 1.40 cr reimburses interest on the Noida plant loans and sits in other income, not in finance costs. It continues while the policy and the loans run, so it is shown as information only.

adjustments.item: Unrealised exchange loss charged to profit
adjustments.reason: The cash-flow add-back of Rs 10.11 cr in FY26 (Rs 1.18 cr FY25) is a non-cash charge that can reverse. With imports at 76.2% of raw material purchases (p. 41), exchange movements are a recurring feature of cost, so it is not added back; it raises earnings if it reverses.

adjustments.item: Borrowing cost capitalised to property, plant and equipment
adjustments.reason: Interest of Rs 1.15 cr (FY26), Rs 0.75 cr (FY25) and Rs 7.25 cr (FY24) was added to asset cost under Ind AS 23 while the Noida and Ganaur plants were being built. This is the standard treatment for qualifying assets; shown for completeness.

earnings_quality.verdict: Reported P/E is a fair measure: the adjustments found move FY26 PAT by -1.0%, within the 10% threshold. On the FY24-FY26 average, which smooths one-year items, the P/E is 85.8x reported and 86.5x adjusted.
flags: Other income of Rs 6.64 cr includes Rs 0.85 cr of liabilities written back, which did not recur in FY25 (nil); 1.1% of PBT. Not part of operating earnings.
checked: Allowance for expected credit loss Rs 0.19 cr against receivables of Rs 218.58 cr (0.09%); 52.8% of receivables are past their due date, 96% of that under six months (p. 337)
Bank-deposit interest Rs 2.41 cr is 3.0% of PBT; service and fee charges Rs 1.60 cr, insurance claim Rs 0.14 cr (p. 346)
Promoter and relative remuneration in FY26: Sagar Gupta Rs 0.88 cr, Chandra Prakash Gupta Rs 1.05 cr, Madhuri Gupta Rs 0.28 cr, relatives Rs 0.18 cr (pp. 78-80); 3.6% of PAT
Deferred tax credit of Rs 0.29 cr in FY26 does not flatter profit (p. 74)
Government capital subsidy of Rs 10.79 cr was deducted from the cost of PPE rather than taken to profit (p. 75)
